messages.subject: Missing valid days in section 4 and 5 output
messages.subject_clean: Missing valid days in section 4 and 5 output
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

I’m using GGIR to process my 7-day actigraph data. I’m getting fewer days of output data in section 4 and 5 compared to section 2. The full 7 days appear in section 2, but only 3 or 4 appear in section 4 and 5. Section 4 and 5 often starts with the day we posted the acti to the participant, has a few missing days when it was in transit then ends at day 7 missing the valid data beyond day 7. I want it to start on the day the participant starts wearing it (usually around day 4) and go for 7 days from that point.

My script is pasted below and milestone data from an example participant can be found here https://www.dropbox.com/s/8zi0lxmh81elvr3/meta_200_ID.RAW.csv.RData?dl=0.

I’ve also tried strategy 2 and 3, editing hrs.del.start depending on when participants started wearing their acti, changing section 5 to be from midnight to midnight (MM) in line with section 2, setting exclude first last day to true and reducing includenight/daycrit.

Any thoughts on what I’m doing wrong? I’m out of ideas of what to try.

Thanks for your time!

Steph

messages.body_plain:
GGIR has been thoroughly tested with GENEActiv .bin files.  Please try to work with the .bin files instead.
I did some effort to facilitate GENEActiv .csv format, but this format changed a couple of times, by which compatibility may have gotten lost.

If working with .bin files is not an option for you then the GGIR code may need to be adapted to work with your data. Either find someone who can do this for you or you can hire me to do this. In the latter case, please contact me and we can discuss further.
Best, Vincent

GGIR in its current form cannot handle epoch aggregated data from ActiLife.

A typical raw data file is at least 20 MB in size and for multi-day recordings even a lot larger.

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Freedson equation
messages.body_plain:
In short, MVPA is calculated based on an acceleration (metric ENMO) threshold you specify as user, which by default is 100.
There is a distinction between bouted and non-bouted MVPA.

The calculation in part 2 was described in  https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/25361583
The calculation in part 5 was described in https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/28367987
Further, you can search the google group and the GGIR package documentation for the term "bout" or "bout metric" to get more information.

For the Freedson equation you need Actigraph counts. Freedson's MVPA calculation is not part of GGIR because GGIR does not calculate or process Actigraphy count data. GGIR was developed to facilitate the processing of raw data accelerometry in order to help the research field to move away from these notorious count data.

Best, Vincent
